sentences: Himalaya Shipping Ltd. is deep sea foreign transportation of  freight, classified by the SEC under "Deep Sea Foreign Transportation of  Freight", based in Bermuda.
It reported $67.8m of revenue over the trailing four quarters, down 4.2% against the same quarter a year earlier, at a gross margin of 76.3%.
Listed on NYSE, it funds itself from operations ($19.8m of operating cash flow over the year).
summary.note: Assembled from filing metadata and XBRL figures. Not editorial judgement - and rule 7 asks whether *you* can explain it, so rewrite this in your own words before you rely on it.

bull.text: Gross margin of 76.3% means most of each additional sale falls through to cover fixed costs.
Operating cash flow is positive at $19.8m over the trailing year, so the business funds itself and is not dependent on raising money.

bear.text: Revenue fell 4.2% year on year (Q2 2025 vs Q2 2024). Whatever the story is, it is not currently showing up in sales.
Gross margin compressed from 82.1% to 76.3% against the same quarter a year earlier. Either input costs are rising or the company is discounting to hold volume.
Diluted share count rose 6.0% over the year (Q2 2025 vs Q2 2024). The company can grow while your share of it shrinks, and this is the number most commentary ignores.
Debt of $689.2m against equity of $161.7m. Leverage decides who controls the outcome if trading deteriorates, and it is not the shareholder.
Only 3 quarters of reported history. There is no track record here to speak of, and a short series flatters whatever the recent trend happens to be.
No officer history could be reconstructed from public filings, so the team - the thing that matters most - is the thing we know least about.
Base rate: 57.8% of US common stocks underperformed one-month Treasury bills over their lifetimes (Bessembinder, Journal of Financial Economics, 2018). Nothing above changes that starting point.
